chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub said, a number of our companions narrated to me, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskan, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Abu Sa'id al-Zuhri, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

It suffices for those possessing understanding — the creation of the Subduing Lord, the Kingdom of the Compelling Lord, the Majesty of the Manifest Lord, the Light of the Dazzling Lord, the proof of the Truthful Lord, what He caused the tongues of the servants to speak with, what He sent the Messengers with, and what He revealed to the servants — as evidence for the Lord.

key_terms.أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ: Those possessing understanding/intellect — a Quranic phrase (e.g., 3:190) denoting those who use their reason
key_terms.الرَّبِّ الظَّاهِرِ: The Manifest Lord — One whose signs are apparent and evident in creation
key_terms.الرَّبِّ الْقَاهِرِ: The Compelling Lord — al-Qahir is a divine name meaning the All-Subduing, Overwhelming
key_terms.الرَّبِّ الْمُسَخِّرِ: The Subduing Lord — One who subjugates and controls all of creation
key_terms.بُرْهَانِ الرَّبِّ الصَّادِقِ: The proof of the Truthful Lord — God's proofs are truthful and reliable

ai.seo_question: What proof does Imam al-Baqir give for the existence of God in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) presents a comprehensive theological argument that sufficient proof of God's existence is available to people of intellect through eight categories of evidence: divine creation, divine sovereignty, divine majesty, divine light, divine proof, the speech He has given to His servants, the mission of the Prophets, and the revealed scriptures. This hadith is from the first chapter of al-Kafi (Kitab al-'Aql wa'l-Jahl), which establishes rational and theological foundations for knowledge of God. The Imam's teaching here reflects the Shia theological emphasis on the role of 'aql (intellect) as a means for recognizing divine truth.
